answer: In an agent economy coordinating timber shipments from a knoll to a harbor, each agent must lock $100 in escrow before bidding. The bond stays locked for 30 days after its last job and is slashed if signed delivery records prove fraud. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up $100,000 for at least a month; using them to cheat risks losing those bonds. New identities cannot erase the capital requirement, so cheap account creation does not buy cheap influence.
